# ADR-014: License: MIT

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-05

## Decision
Jaari is released under the MIT License (`LICENSE`). Code reused from MIT-licensed references (`pi`, `open-instinct`) keeps its upstream copyright and permission notice in `NOTICE`, with the source path and pinned commit. `gajae-way` (AGPL-3.0-only) is a design reference only, because copying its code would force Jaari under AGPL. `openinstinct` has no license and is a behavioral spec only (ADR-009); this includes its `daemon/src/memory/vendor/` files, which are copies of gajae-way code. Techniques openinstinct adapted from MIT projects (e.g. beeper/platform-imessage) are taken from the upstream project with its notice, never via openinstinct. New dependencies must be MIT-compatible (MIT, BSD, ISC, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, MPL-2.0 at file level); AGPL/SSPL services run only as separate processes.

## Alternatives rejected
Apache-2.0 (patent grant and NOTICE mechanism, but heavier for plugin authors and a mismatch with the MIT references); AGPL-3.0 (would allow copying gajae-way, but puts copyleft on every plugin and self-hoster who modifies Jaari); no license (nobody could legally use or contribute).
